lessons.title: Unit 1 – Lesson 1: A fire at Mariem’s building
match: Unit 1 – Lesson 1: A fire at Mariem’s building
objectives: Talk and ask about past actions and events.
Form the simple past of regular and irregular verbs.
Tell a past experience in a short paragraph.
lessons.intro: Have you ever seen a fire? What happened?
lessons.summary: At the office, Mariem tells Moctar and Abdoul that there was a fire in her building the night before: some old stuff in the basement burned. She smelt something burning while she was coming close to the building, saw smoke as she was getting in, and called the firemen. They asked everybody to evacuate the building and dealt with the fire. Luckily, there was no serious damage.
points: Simple past: regular verbs + -ed (called, played).
Spelling: carry → carried; like → liked.
Irregular verbs: break → broke, get → got, go → went, see → saw.
Question: How did it happen? / Negative: It didn’t …

application.q: What did Mariem tell Moctar and Abdoul?
application.a: That there was a fire in her building.

lessons.title: Unit 1 – Lesson 2: At work
objectives: Talk about past actions in progress.
Use the past continuous tense.

lessons.intro: Is it a problem to be late at school or at work? Why?
lessons.summary: At 10 o’clock, Mohamed, a clerk, was standing in front of the office of Mr Brahim, the company manager. He was late as usual, tense and afraid. When he got in, the boss, who was writing at his desk, stared at him and asked why he was always late. Mohamed explained that he had come at eight, prepared the letters for the customers and gone out to have tea. The boss accepted but reminded him that he should always inform the secretary before going out.
points: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing.
Used for an action in progress in the past: Mohamed was standing…
Opposites: in front of ≠ behind, to get in ≠ to get out.

lessons.title: Unit 2 – Lesson 1: Brahim’s hometown
objectives: Describe a place and people in the past.
Use the past progressive (affirmative, negative, questions).
Write about one’s hometown.
lessons.intro: What do you know about Chinguetti?
lessons.summary: Brahim lives in Nouakchott, but when he was young he used to live in Chinguetti, an ancient Islamic town in northern Mauritania. It was pretty and clean; there were beautiful old houses, many old and famous libraries and a splendid mosque of stone and mud, visited by people from remote places. People were friendly and open-minded, and there were lovely small inns for tourists. But being in the desert, most houses of the ancient section were almost buried under dunes, and people were always pushing the dunes back while sand storms kept covering the town.
points: Past progressive: was/were + verb-ing.
Negative: was not (wasn’t) / were not (weren’t).
Questions: Were you speaking? – Yes, I was / No, I wasn’t.
Used to + verb: past habit (I used to live in Chinguetti).

lessons.title: Unit 2 – Lesson 2: The two friends
objectives: Describe people’s appearance and character.
Form adverbs of manner (adjective + -ly).
Compare two people.
lessons.intro: Describe your best friend in three words.
lessons.summary: Mohamed and Ali, from Nouakchott, are neighbours and classmates, about 17 years old; they speak English fluently. Mohamed is tall with long black hair; Ali is rather short with curly bushy hair. Their characters differ: Mohamed is shy, speaks slowly, moves carefully, seldom gets angry, but has a strong character; he is kind, generous, prays at the mosque and obeys his parents. Ali is good-looking, always smiling, daring and stubborn; he is sometimes aggressive, but kind and obedient to his mother. Both recited the Koran young, and they are inseparable.
points: Physical description: tall, short, long black hair, curly hair.
Character: shy, kind, generous, daring, stubborn, obedient.
Contrast: whereas, however, but.
Adverbs of manner: fluent → fluently, careful → carefully.

application.a: They are neighbours, classmates and close friends.

lessons.title: Unit 2 – Lesson 3: Visiting Nouakchott
objectives: Describe places with adjectives and actions with adverbs.
Understand basic facts about HIV and its prevention.
Write a short paragraph on prevention.
lessons.intro: What important places would you show a visitor in Nouakchott?
lessons.summary: Meima visits her cousin Aissata in Nouakchott. Driving to the beach, they pass the National Hospital (big compared to the village dispensary), the tuberculosis centre and the HIV centre. Aissata explains that being infected does not necessarily mean being sick: one can live with the virus without symptoms; HIV-positive people must take their medicines regularly to slow down the disease, and AIDS treatment is free. The virus is transmitted through blood transfusion or sexual intercourse. To avoid it: religion forbids sexual intercourse outside marriage, and doctors advise prevention methods; radio and TV programmes deal with the issue.
points: Adjectives describe things: big, good, beautiful.
Adverbs of manner describe actions: carefully, slowly, regularly.
HIV: infected ≠ always sick; treatment is free.
Prevention: religion, medical advice, awareness programmes.

application.a: Aissata’s cousin, visiting Nouakchott from her village.

lessons.intro: What do candidates usually promise during a campaign?
lessons.summary: Aicha attended a presidential campaign meeting of the opposition; Leila couldn’t go because she wasn’t feeling well. Aicha says the meeting was crowded and exciting and the candidate brilliant. He said he would improve living conditions (lower food prices, higher salaries), build schools, roads and hospitals, reinforce security, national unity, justice and equality, and pay more attention to girls’ schooling and women’s participation. Leila doesn’t believe politicians’ promises because once elected they often forget them; Aicha thinks some are honest.

lessons.intro: Where would you like to spend your summer holidays?
lessons.summary: After passing their exams, Mohamed and Haroun plan their holidays. lessons.title: Unit 4: A frightening experience
objectives: Express simultaneous past actions.

lessons.intro: Have you ever been really frightened? What happened?
lessons.summary: Fatma tells Noura about her frightening night. She was watching TV when she heard a scream and a crash: someone had broken into the flat and surprised her maid Amy, who fell unconscious. While Fatma was calling her neighbour Ali, a policeman, she heard footsteps coming towards her room. She called her maid’s name, in vain. Then she saw her husband Salem and was relieved: while he was visiting his parents, his boss had called him back, and he couldn’t phone because the network was bad.
points: Past continuous: long action in progress; simple past: short event.

lessons.intro: What does your family usually do in the evening?
lessons.summary: Yesterday at eight, Mr Sidi was reading a newspaper while his wife Aicha was cleaning the tea set; their daughters Leila and Navissa were reciting Koran verses written on their tablets. Sidi’s friend Camara came in and was welcomed warmly. While the two men were chatting about social issues, Aicha was preparing tea in another room. The baby Ahmed woke up and cried because he didn’t see his mother; disturbed, the men went to the garden to talk peacefully.
points: Past continuous: was/were + verb-ing for actions in progress.
While + past continuous for simultaneous actions.
Adverbs of manner: warmly, calmly, peacefully.

lessons.title: Unit 6 – Lesson 2: Mustafa’s life
objectives: Express duration with the present perfect (for, since).
Use already and yet.

lessons.intro: Would you prefer to live in the city or in your village later?
lessons.summary: Mustafa grew up in the south. After high school he studied at the University of Nouakchott, got a scholarship to study abroad, and came back to teach at the University of Nouakchott. His hobby was gardening (his friends called him the “amateur gardener”); it reminded him of the countryside. Married, he planted his first real garden in his big house. He has taught at the university for eight years and is well-known, but now he is tired of fame; he hasn’t decided yet to move to the countryside, but he has already chosen a place near Mederdra, his hometown.
points: Present perfect + already (positive) / yet (negative, questions).
For + length of time; since + starting point.
Mauritania has been independent since 1960.

lessons.title: Unit 6 – Lesson 3: Pollution
objectives: Use the past perfect tense.
Explain the causes and effects of pollution.
Write a paragraph about reducing pollution.
lessons.intro: What pollutes the air and the water in your town?
lessons.summary: Aly, who used to live in a remote area of the countryside, now lives in Nouakchott and is amazed by all the fuss about pollution. His elder sister Amy explains: pollution is the fumes and chemical substances in the air we breathe, the water we drink and the products we eat, which threaten our lives. They come from plants, factories, car and plane exhausts. Dead fish floating on the sea show sea pollution; air pollution causes respiratory problems (asthma, bronchitis); land pollution destroys forests and vegetation. Aly agrees that something must be done.
points: Past perfect: had + past participle.
Negative: had not; question: Had they…?
Pollution: air, water (sea), land.
Causes: factories, cars, planes, chemical substances.
